## The data

This TidyTuesday dataset (February 18, 2020) comes from nu3's Food
Carbon Footprint Index 2018, which uses FAO data to estimate how much of
each food category people eat in 130 countries and the CO2 emissions
tied to that consumption. Each row is one country and one food category
(for example beef, rice, or milk), with consumption in kg per person per
year and emissions in kg of CO2 per person per year. Kasia Kulma scraped
and cleaned the data for TidyTuesday.

## Plot

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

food <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2020/2020-02-18/food_consumption.csv")

food |>
  group_by(food_category) |>
  summarize(median_co2 = median(co2_emmission)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = median_co2, y = fct_reorder(food_category, median_co2))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#1F4E4A") +
  labs(
    x = "Median CO2 emissions across countries (kg per person per year)",
    y = NULL,
    title = "Beef and dairy have the largest footprints per person"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
